evidence.claim: The Prime Minister heads the Cabinet and executive power is exercised by or under the authority of the Prime Minister; the President appoints the MP who commands a parliamentary majority.
evidence.title: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Bangladesh
evidence.publication_date: n.d. consolidated text in force in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Prime Minister heads the Cabinet and executive power is exercised by or under the authority of the Prime Minister; the President appoints the MP who commands a parliamentary majority.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text from the official legal repository.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sheikh Hasina's office and formal authority, but not to any specific 2022 nuclear-risk decision.
contrary_evidence: Formal executive authority does not prove responsible use of that authority in any specific year.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh is listed as a TPNW signatory and party, with ratification recorded in 2019 and the treaty in force from 22 January 2021.
evidence.title: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons - status and participant actions
evidence.publication_date: status page current; treaty adopted 2017; Bangladesh ratification recorded 2019
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh is listed as a TPNW signatory and party, with ratification recorded in 2019 and the treaty in force from 22 January 2021.
evidence.source_locator: Status table for chapter XXVI, treaty 9
evidence.period_fit: Background treaty posture that was fully in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State action under Hasina's government; not a personal act in 2022, but it defines the inherited non-nuclear posture.
contrary_evidence: Treaty adherence is a formal commitment, not proof of implementation quality in a specific year.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh submitted its Article 2 declaration to the UN on 21 February 2021.
evidence.title: Declarations pursuant to Article 2 of the TPNW
evidence.publisher: United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh submitted its Article 2 declaration to the UN on 21 February 2021.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 formal compliance record that remained operative in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State compliance under Hasina's government; indirect but relevant to 2022 posture.
contrary_evidence: The table confirms filing, not the substantive contents of the declaration.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh's Article 2 declaration stated that it does not own, possess, or control nuclear weapons, has never done so, and does not host any other state's nuclear weapons on its territory.
evidence.title: Bangladesh | Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.publisher: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons
evidence.publication_date: crawled 2025; content refers to 2021 declaration and 2022 implementation
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh's Article 2 declaration stated that it does not own, possess, or control nuclear weapons, has never done so, and does not host any other state's nuclear weapons on its territory.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized treaty-monitoring NGO with direct treaty-status compilation; strong but not primary like UN text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State declaration under Hasina's government; not a personal 2022 decision, but highly relevant to the ruler-period posture.
contrary_evidence: This is a self-reported declaration and should be treated as baseline compliance, not proof of broader restraint across all risk domains.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh has a comprehensive safeguards agreement in force from 1982 and an Additional Protocol in force from 2001.
evidence.title: Country List : Office of Legal Affairs : IAEA
evidence.publication_date: crawled 2026; treaty dates shown in record
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh has a comprehensive safeguards agreement in force from 1982 and an Additional Protocol in force from 2001.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level regulatory posture under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: Safeguards existence does not show whether all domestic safety or security practices were optimal in 2022.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh stated that total elimination of nuclear weapons is the ultimate guarantee of security, reaffirmed support for TPNW, NPT, and CTBT, and said it was proceeding with its nuclear power plant in line with the highest IAEA standards.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement Hepr Thematic Debate: “Nuclear Weapons”
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh stated that total elimination of nuclear weapons is the ultimate guarantee of security, reaffirmed support for TPNW, NPT, and CTBT, and said it was proceeding with its nuclear power plant in line with the highest IAEA standards.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary diplomatic statement from Bangladesh's UN mission during 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and squarely on nuclear-disarmament posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: National position under Hasina's government; the statement is institutional rather than a direct personal quote, but it reflects the government's line.
contrary_evidence: The statement is normative and aspirational; it does not by itself prove concrete safety improvements or operational restraint in the civilian program.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh warned that rapid technological advances, including artificial intelligence and biotechnology, could pose risks to international peace and security and urged vigilance against malicious use of such technologies.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement Counsellor Thematic Debate: “Other Disarmament Measures And International Security”
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh warned that rapid technological advances, including artificial intelligence and biotechnology, could pose risks to international peace and security and urged vigilance against malicious use of such technologies.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to catastrophic dual-use governance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level position under Hasina's government; not proof of a ruler-specific operational decision, but relevant to policy stance.
contrary_evidence: This is a broad multilateral statement, not a Bangladesh-specific domestic control action.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh called for immediate cessation of hostilities in Ukraine, urged restraint by all parties, and asked for a return to diplomacy and dialogue.
evidence.title: 2022 Statement DPR Ukraine Crisis
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh called for immediate cessation of hostilities in Ukraine, urged restraint by all parties, and asked for a return to diplomacy and dialogue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 diplomatic statement from Bangladesh at the UN.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to crisis de-escalation norms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level foreign-policy stance under Hasina's government; indirect attribution only.
contrary_evidence: The statement is general diplomacy, not evidence of a ruler personally managing a nuclear crisis.
It does not involve nuclear command-and-control.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh had two nuclear power reactors under construction at Rooppur and no nuclear electricity production recorded in the PRIS summary.
evidence.title: Bangladesh country details
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh had two nuclear power reactors under construction at Rooppur and no nuclear electricity production recorded in the PRIS summary.
evidence.period_fit: The construction status is consistent with the 2022 period and helps define exposure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State infrastructure context under Hasina's government, not evidence of individual risk conduct.
contrary_evidence: Construction status alone says nothing about safety quality or political judgment.

evidence.claim: An IAEA expert mission concluded that Bangladesh is committed to continuous improvement of nuclear and radiation safety, while also identifying areas for possible improvement in the regulatory framework.
evidence.title: IAEA says Bangladesh committed to continuous improvement of nuclear and radiation safety
evidence.excerpt: An IAEA expert mission concluded that Bangladesh is committed to continuous improvement of nuclear and radiation safety, while also identifying areas for possible improvement in the regulatory framework.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical specialist reporting based on the IAEA mission outcome, but still a secondary source.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and closely tied to Rooppur and safety governance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to Hasina's government through the national regulatory system; not a personal action statement.
contrary_evidence: The same mission identified areas for improvement in policy, legal framework, and human resources.

evidence.claim: At the Rooppur Unit 2 reactor-pressure-vessel installation ceremony, Sheikh Hasina said the government would continue supplying electricity despite austerity pressures from the Russia-Ukraine war, sanctions, and inflation.
evidence.title: People will get electricity, but should be economical in use: PM
evidence.excerpt: At the Rooppur Unit 2 reactor-pressure-vessel installation ceremony, Sheikh Hasina said the government would continue supplying electricity despite austerity pressures from the Russia-Ukraine war, sanctions, and inflation.
evidence.source_locator: Article text describing the ceremony and quoting the PM
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting with a direct ruler quote and a specific dated event.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to a major nuclear-energy milestone.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sheikh Hasina as PM.
contrary_evidence: The event concerns energy policy and project momentum, not nuclear-weapon risk.
The quote reflects adaptation to external shocks rather than proof of safety success.

evidence.claim: Western sanctions on Russia created fears that financing and transactions for the Rooppur nuclear power plant could be disrupted because the project depended on Russian banking and suppliers.
evidence.title: Western sanctions cast a cloud over Russia-backed Bangladesh nuclear power plant
evidence.excerpt: Western sanctions on Russia created fears that financing and transactions for the Rooppur nuclear power plant could be disrupted because the project depended on Russian banking and suppliers.
evidence.source_locator: Opening paragraphs describing VEB, SWIFT, and the project financing risk
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable local reporting, but still a secondary and contingent risk assessment rather than a definitive outcome record.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within early 2022, when Ukraine-war sanctions affected the project environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Constraint on Hasina's government rather than a choice fully under its control; relevant to inherited risk and exposure.
contrary_evidence: This is a risk report, not proof that the project was mismanaged or that a nuclear-safety failure occurred.
